title: Dispatch: M1-M12 packet-intervention evidence suite (attempt 1)
description:
Dispatch 4 of 4 for W10 (`eshyra-o9bd.19.12`, ADR 0020 transition design
sections 12.3, 13.1, 13.3). Parent authority: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.12`;
design authority
`docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md`.

WORKTREE `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.12.4`, BRANCH `eshyra-o9bd.19.12.4`, cut
from `eshyra-o9bd.19.12` AFTER the seam dispatch `eshyra-o9bd.19.12.3` merged
into it. Dependencies are installed. Touch nothing outside it.

## What already exists on your base branch

Read all of it before writing a line:

- `packages/core/src/discovery/packetMessage.ts` —
  `renderContextPacketMessage`, and `packetMessage.test.ts` for how a packet is
  built from a probe fixture through the real offline harness.
- `packages/core/src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts` — the `discoveryMode`
  dep (`off` | `shadow` | `intervene`) and the injection point.
- `packages/core/src/discovery/shadow.ts` — `captureDiscoveryIntervention`,
  schema `discovery-shadow-v2`, its fail-closed reader, and `ShadowDelivery`.
- `packages/core/src/discovery/measurements.ts` — `measureDiscovery` (M1-M9),
  `measureRuntimeDiscovery` (M10, M11), `measureAcceptedStateEffect` (M12).
- `packages/core/test/discovery/shadowRuntime.test.ts` — `RUNTIME_REACH`, the
  per-execution probe loop, `ScriptedModel`, `StructuredScriptedModel`,
  `ScriptedAuditor`, `recordedEvidence`, `requireTrace`, `requireRuntime`, and
  the support installers.
- `packages/core/test/diagnostics/` — the twelve fixtures, and
  `expectedDeterministicStateEffect.operations` (design section 11.2).

## What this dispatch delivers, and nothing more

The intervention evidence suite. You add ONE new test file and may export
shared helpers from existing test modules so the two suites cannot pin
different tables. You change NO production code. If the seam looks wrong,
record it with `bd update eshyra-o9bd.19.12.4 --append-notes` and file a
follow-up with `bd create` — do not fix it here.

## Deliverable 5 — the permanent evidence

New file `packages/core/test/discovery/packetIntervention.test.ts`. It is the
bead's permanent evidence and must actually REPORT M1–M12 per probe, not merely
assert that nothing failed (§13.3).

Structure it as the existing per-execution loop in `shadowRuntime.test.ts`
does — every fixture, every execution, using `installScenarioBinding`,
`installJhptCampaignRules`, `installProbeCampaignState`. For each execution run
TWO turns on two freshly seeded databases with the same scripted model, the same
auditor and the same seed: the BASELINE in `'shadow'` mode, then the
INTERVENTION in `'intervene'` mode. Read both evidences back OUT OF SQLITE and
measure from the re-read evidence, never from an in-memory object.

Assert, per execution:

E1. **Baseline parity of discovery itself.** M1–M9 computed from the
    intervention evidence deep-equal those computed from the baseline evidence,
    and M1/M2 equal the pinned `RUNTIME_REACH` table for that label. Injection
    changes what the DM receives; it must not change what discovery found.
    Import the existing table rather than copying it — export it from
    `shadowRuntime.test.ts` or move it to a shared support module, so the two
    suites cannot pin different tables.
E2. **The packet reached the DM, additively.** The intervention run's model
    input contains the baseline run's rendered context as an exact prefix, and
    the remainder equals the rendered packet text. Assert against the model
    client's captured `ModelCompleteInput`, not against the trace alone.
E3. **The trace records what was sent.** `turn_trace.retrieved_context` for the
    intervention turn equals the message the model actually received, and the
    evidence's `delivery.renderedSha256` is the SHA-256 of the packet portion of
    that message.
E4. **Provider neutrality.** Run one probe's intervention turn twice — once
    with the fenced-text `ScriptedModel` and once with the native-transport
    `StructuredScriptedModel` — and assert the injected packet text is
    byte-identical across both. This is the bead's provider-neutrality claim and
    must be proven, not asserted in prose.
E5. **Source prose reached the DM verbatim.** For every fixture field-9 entry
    carrying an `exactSubstring` whose target actually reached the packet,
    assert the substring appears unescaped in the message the model received.
    Report which field-9 facts were checked per probe so an empty check set
    cannot read as green.
E6. **Partial-projection limits are in band in the DELIVERED message.** Prove
    both design §7.2 worked cases end to end: `creature:adult-black-dragon`
    (P3) success-branch-and-area omission and `spell:fireball` (P4) missing
    typed area, each note appearing between its own candidate's heading and the
    next candidate's heading in the delivered text.
E7. **No laundering (P12).** The delivered message never presents
    `table:starting-wealth-by-class` as authority: M8's `forbiddenPresent` and
    `unattributedPresent` are both empty, and the string does not appear in the
    delivered text under any authority framing.
E8. **Capability presentation.** P8's delivered text carries the positive
    bounded contract (operation, revision, inputs, exclusions, residual
    interpretation) matching the fixture's `expectedCapabilityStatus`; a probe
    whose fixture declares `none-selected` carries the negative form and its
    disclaimer, and never the words "no mechanics" or "safe to ignore" as a
    conclusion.
E9. **Campaign rules and rulings.** For P7's `with-active-ruling` execution and
    P10's house rule, the delivered text carries identity, kind, campaign
    scope, provenance, effective position and supersession status beside the
    governing source material, matching what M5 reports as placed.
E10. **M6 overflow.** Assert per probe that `mustConsiderOverflow` is empty AND
    that the gate is not vacuous: add one case that forces an overflow through a
    reduced budget and asserts the probe fails — the overflow record names the
    candidate and its routes, the delivered text discloses it, and the
    measurement reports the failure. The parent's required next state is "no
    must-consider overflow occurred, OR every occurrence failed its probe as
    designed"; this case proves the second half is real.
E11. **M10, M11, M12.** M10 and M11 from `measureRuntimeDiscovery`, and M12 from
    `measureAcceptedStateEffect` against the execution's own
    `expectedDeterministicStateEffect`. Every execution reports M12. For the
    eleven `none` executions assert `agreed` with an empty disagreement list;
    for P8 drive a scripted `use_item` call and assert `agreed` against the
    fixture's declared `operations`. A probe whose M12 disagrees fails.
E12. **The non-claim.** The evidence's `modelUsageClaim` is `null`, the
    rendered packet's is `null`, and the per-probe report carries no field that
    asserts the model used the material. Assert structurally that the report
    object has no coverage, readiness, completeness, score or rate field, and
    that M1–M12 are reported independently and are never summed or averaged
    across probes (§13.2). A count of probes passing is permitted; a rate is
    not.

Build the per-probe report as an explicit object holding M1–M12 and assert it
against pinned expected values. "Nothing threw" is not a pass.


## Non-negotiables

- `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing.
- Biome is canonical; CI fails on warnings. Do not suppress a finding.
- Do not weaken, skip, or reshape any existing test.
- Do not edit `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, anything under `.claude/`, or the
  design document.
- `npm run verify:worktree` intermittently fails
  `packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts > packs publishable tarballs` on a 10s timeout
  under full-suite load. That is a known pre-existing flake
  (`bd list` it under the CLI packaging bug) and is unrelated to your change:
  confirm it passes with `npx vitest run packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts` and say
  so in your notes. Do NOT "fix" it and do not let it stop you committing.

PER-PROBE M1-M12, what the suite actually found (all 13 executions: 12 fixtures,
P7 authoring two):

- E1 (baseline parity): M1-M9 (and the rest of DiscoveryMeasurements) computed from
  the intervention evidence deep-equal those from the baseline evidence for every one
  of the 13 executions, and M1/M2 equal the imported RUNTIME_REACH table exactly.
  Confirms the seam's core claim: injection changes what the DM receives, never what
  discovery found.
- E2/E3 (additive delivery + trace binding): held for all 13 -- intervention message
  = baseline message + '\n\n' + packet text; Buffer.byteLength(packetText) ==
  delivery.renderedBytes; sha256(packetText) == delivery.renderedSha256; and
  turn_trace.retrieved_context == [the exact message the model received], all read
  back out of SQLite.
- E4 (provider neutrality): P3's injected packet text is byte-identical between the
  fenced ScriptedModel transport and the native StructuredScriptedModel transport, and
  each independently matches its own recorded renderedSha256.
- E5 (field-9 substrings in the delivered message): pinned per-label checked counts
  (0 for P1, P2, P5 -- their exactSubstring targets are lost at the runtime `signals`
  stage per RUNTIME_REACH, matching W9's known signal-extraction gap; 0 for P9/P11/P12
  which declare no exactSubstring facts; 1-2 for P3/P4/P6/P7(x2)/P8/P10 where the
  target does reach). Every checked fact's exactSubstring appears verbatim, unescaped,
  in the model's actual input.
- E6 (partial-projection worked cases, end to end): P3's dragon block (creature:
  adult-black-dragon) carries the success-branch-omission note beside
  /data/actions/5/mechanics/saves and the missing-typed-area note; P4's fireball block
  carries the missing-typed-area note positioned between its Typed projection and
  Deterministic capability headings. Both in the DELIVERED text, not an offline-only
  render.
- E7 (P12 no laundering): M8 forbiddenPresent/unattributedPresent both empty, and
  'table:starting-wealth-by-class' does not appear anywhere in the delivered message.
- E8 (capability presentation): positive form (POSITIVE BOUNDED CONTRACT,
  operation=hit-target, revision=derived-magic-item-clauses-v1, status=available,
  required inputs/exclusions/residual interpretation all present) proven through the
  OFFLINE harness for P8, using the SAME renderContextPacketMessage the live seam
  calls. NOT provable through the live intervene round trip: real campaign state
  carries no literal operationId leaf for an item instance (signals.ts requires one to
  fire the capability-preflight signal), and installProbeCampaignState deliberately
  does not synthesize it -- the identical "don't hand the signals stage the answer"
  policy that already governs P1/P2's documented runtime loss. So P8's LIVE delivered
  packet carries the negative form too, pinned explicitly rather than silently
  differing from the offline suite. Filed as follow-up eshyra-o9bd.19.12.6 (P3 for
  P3's genuine live negative-form proof + full "never as a conclusion" check on "no
  mechanics"/"safe to ignore" -- every occurrence of both phrases in the delivered
  text is inside the renderer's fixed disclaiming sentence, counted and compared, not
  merely asserted).
- E9 (campaign rules/rulings beside governing material): P7/with-active-ruling and
  P10/default both carry identity (matched exactly against what M5 reports as
  `placed`), kind, status, scope, provenance, effective position, supersededBy,
  revokedPosition (P7 additionally: ambiguity id + selected interpretation id) inside
  the SAME candidate block as the governing source record, in the delivered text.
- E10 (must-consider overflow gate): first half -- all 13 executions report
  mustConsiderOverflow empty and the shared assertProbePassesM6 gate does not trip.
  Second half (the load-bearing negative case) -- a dedicated offline-harness test
  reduces P9's budget to maxCandidates:1, forces a real overflow (candidate + real
  non-empty routes), confirms the delivered text discloses it under '## Must-consider
  overflow' with the candidate key and every route class, confirms
  rendered.mustConsiderOverflow's length matches measureDiscovery's m6.overflow
  length, and proves assertProbePassesM6 throws over exactly this case -- the same
  gate every other execution is proven NOT to trip. This is the proof the parent's
  "no overflow occurred, OR every occurrence failed its probe" acceptance needs both
  halves of.
- E11 (M10/M11/M12): auditorAbsent=true, retries=0 for all 13 (no auditor wired,
  matching the suite's baseline/intervention symmetry requirement). M10: for the 12
  non-P8 executions every comparison (where any exist) reports runtimeOutcome
  'not-invoked' and runtimeInvocationsAbsentFromPacket is empty (nothing was invoked).
  For P8, m10.comparisons is empty (the packet never preflighted anything -- see E8
  finding above) and runtimeInvocationsAbsentFromPacket contains exactly the scripted
  use_item(ammunition-stack-1, hit-target) invocation -- matches the pre-existing
  Phase-2 finding in shadowRuntime.test.ts. M12: all 12 none-declaring executions
  agree with an empty disagreement list and an empty accepted-effects set; P8 (the
  one execution with a real declared effect, Amendment D) drives a real scripted
  use_item call against the exact instanceId/operationId its own fixture declares
  (installProbeCampaignState seeds instanceId 'ammunition-stack-1', matching the
  fixture verbatim, so no operation-only-comparable workaround was needed) and agrees
  fully, with a non-empty accepted-effects set.
- E12 (non-claim): evidence.modelUsageClaim is null for every execution; every
  per-probe report object was checked structurally for any key matching
  coverage/readiness/completeness/score/rate -- the only hit anywhere in 13 reports
  was M5's ambiguityCoverage (a categorical seam-query-scope enum, all-active vs
  requested-ambiguities, never a numeric figure), named and excluded explicitly, with
  its value independently asserted to be exactly that enum so the exception can't go
  vacuous. The delivered text was also checked against coverage/completeness/percentage/
  "model used" language for every execution. A final aggregate test confirms
  PROBE_REPORTS.length === 13, computes a passing COUNT (not a rate), and structurally
  re-checks the aggregate object for the same forbidden fields -- nothing in the suite
  computes a quotient over probes.

SPEC ITEMS I COULD NOT DO AS LITERALLY WRITTEN: the dispatch's E8 line ("P8's
delivered text carries the positive bounded contract... matching the fixture's
expectedCapabilityStatus") is not achievable through the live runTurn/intervene round
trip as the seam is currently wired -- see the E8 finding above and follow-up
eshyra-o9bd.19.12.6. I proved the positive form through the offline harness instead
(reusing the exact same renderer function intervention injects) and proved P8's real
negative form as an explicit, pinned fact rather than silently omitting the mismatch.
I also noted the dispatch's prose says "the eleven none executions" for E11; the
actual corpus has TWELVE none-declaring executions plus P8's one effect execution
(13 total, matching the pre-existing 'runs every authored fixture execution' test's
own assertion that authored.length > DIAGNOSTIC_FIXTURES.length). This is a minor
wording slip in the spec, not a seam defect; implemented against the real corpus data.

CONCERN ABOUT THE SEAM: none beyond the E8/eshyra-o9bd.19.12.6 finding above. The
intervention seam itself (discoveryMode union, captureDiscoveryIntervention,
ShadowDelivery, the v2 fail-closed reader) behaved exactly as documented in every
case this suite exercises, including its own capture-failure and additive-delivery
guarantees (already covered by shadowRuntime.test.ts and re-confirmed here across the
whole corpus). RunTurnDeps/ShadowDiscoveryInput expose no way to override the
retention budget, which is why E10's forced-overflow case had to go through the
offline stage harness (runDiscoveryStages + the SAME renderContextPacketMessage
production intervention uses) rather than a live runTurn round trip; I judged this
in-scope rather than a follow-up, since it proves the shared renderer/measurement
mechanism directly and packetMessage.test.ts already established the same pattern for
Phase-1 evidence.
